messages.content: Resuming an intermittent failure investigation now.

Most of yesterday disappeared into a 30% error rate on the payment callback. scripts/repro.py grew by a couple hundred lines. A timeline of the incident from the metrics held up fine through the whole load test.
How is an intermittent failure investigation going?
A permanent fix replacing the hotfix keeps getting pushed to next sprint. Capturing a heap profile during the spike is behind us now.
Increasing the connection pool as a stopgap feels like the right fit here.
Here's where things stand. Makes sense, doing that. Nobody needs to think about adding structured logging around the suspect path anymore.
Had to untangle tests/test_regression.py first. Nothing is waiting on anyone at the moment.

src/handlers/checkout.py grew by a couple hundred lines. Once the release settles, backfilling the corrupted rows is where attention goes. Flaky jobs get one automatic retry. The hotfix reverting the connection pool change held up fine through the whole load test.
I keep coming back to a blameless postmortem format.
Bisecting the regression to a single commit came off the board this morning. Fine by me. We can't call this finished while a follow-up on the third-party client bug report is missing.
Ruling out the cache layer as the cause held up fine through the whole load test. Nothing is waiting on anyone at the moment.
After review I'll deploy. Turns out the slowdown was silent data loss when the queue consumer crashed all along.
